XXI.}}</noinclude>into Syria, and came to Tyre: for there the ship vvas to discharge her lode. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=4}}† And finding disciples, vve taried there seuen daies: vvho said to Paul by the Spirit, that he should not goe vp to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=5}}† And the daies being expired, departing vve went forvvard, al bringing vs on the vvay, vvith their vviues and children, til vve vvere out of the citie: and falling vpon our knees on the shore, vve praied. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=6}}† And vvhen vve had bid one an other farevvel, vve vvent vp into the ship: and they returned vnto their owne.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=7}}† But we hauing ended the nauigation, from Tyre came dovvne to Ptolomáis: and saluting the brethren, vve taried one day with them.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=8}}† And the next day departing, vve came to Cæsaréa.

And entring into the house of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 6, 5.''}}* Philip the Euangelist, vvho vvas one of the seuen, vve taried with him. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=9}}† And he had {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ As S. Peter had a wife, but vsed her not after his calling, as it is noted els where out of S. Hierom ''Luc. 4, 38'': so may it be said of S. Philip being Deacon.}}∷ foure daughters {{sup|‖}} virgins, that did prophecie. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=10}}† And as we abode there for certaine daies, there came a certaine prophet from Ievvrie, named Agabus. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=11}}† He, when he was come to vs, tooke Paules girdle: and binding his owne handes & feete, he said, Thus saith the holy Ghost: The man whose girdle this is, so shal the Iewes binde in Hierusalem, & shal deliuer him into the handes of the Gentiles. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=12}}† Which when vve had heard, vve & they that vvere of the same place, desired him that he would not goe vp to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=13}}† Then Paul ansvvered, and said, What doe you, vveeping and afflicting my hart? for I am ready not only to be bound, but to die also in Hierusalem for the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=14}}† And vvhen vve could not persuade him, we ceased, saying, The vvil of our Lord be done.

{{verse|chapter=21|verse=15}}† And after these daies, being prepared, vve vvent vp to Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=16}}† And there came also of the disciples from Cæsaréa vvith vs, bringing with them one Iason a Cyprian (vvith vvhom vve should lodge) an old disciple. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=17}}† And when vve vvere come to Hierusalem, the brethren receiued vs gladly. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=18}}† And the day folovving Paul vvent in vvith vs to Iames, and al the Auncients vvere assembled. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=19}}† Vvhom vvhen he had saluted, he told particularly vvhat God had done among the Gentiles by his ministerie. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=20}}† But they hearing it, magnified God, and said to him: Thou seest (brother) how many thousands there are among the Ievves that haue beleeued: and al are zelátours of the Lavv. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=21}}† But they haue heard of thee that thou doest teach those Iewes<noinclude>{{rh|||that}}</noinclude>
